papers.title: Laser Engineered Slippery Liquid Infused Porous Surfaces (SLIPS) on 3D Printed Metal Alloys
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) inherently produces metallic surfaces with high roughness and porosity, which limits their direct use in applications requiring low interfacial adhesion and controlled liquid mobility. In this work, a scalable strategy is presented for fabricating slippery liquid-infused porous surfaces (SLIPS) directly on as-printed L-PBF Ti6Al4V and AlSi10Mg alloys. Laser surface texturing using nanosecond and picosecond pulsed lasers was employed to restructure the irregular AM surface topography into well-defined microchannel networks that act as capillary reservoirs for lubricant retention. Following fluorosilane functionalization and silicone oil infusion, the resulting SLIPS exhibited static water contact angles exceeding 105° and sliding angles below 10°. Compared with untreated and laser-textured substrates, ice adhesion strength was reduced from approximately 370–460 kPa to ~65 kPa for Ti6Al4V and ~90 kPa for AlSi10Mg. The fabricated SLIPS maintained stable performance during repeated icing and deicing cycles and after mechanical abrasion, thermal exposure, and ultraviolet irradiation, indicating good durability and self-replenishing behavior. Overall, this work demonstrates a direct and versatile route for integrating SLIPS functionality with additively manufactured metal alloys, bridging L-PBF and laser surface engineering to enable durable anti-icing surfaces for aerospace, marine, and energy applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于钛合金表面功能化而非力学或疲劳性能，与研究方向不相关。
llm.why_not_core: No mechanical (tensile, fatigue, hardness) characterization or modeling of Ti-6Al-4V; paper solely concerns surface wettability and anti-icing functionality.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高3D打印金属表面抗冰性能。
summary_zh.method: 在L-PBF Ti6Al4V表面进行激光织构并注入润滑液。
summary_zh.result: 获得低冰粘附力（~65 kPa）和良好耐久性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过接触角、滑动角、冰粘附强度及循环耐久性测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To address the high roughness and porosity of as-printed L-PBF surfaces and enable low-adhesion anti-icing functionality.
summary_en.method: Laser surface texturing with nanosecond and picosecond pulsed lasers was applied to restructure AM surface topography into microchannel networks, followed by fluorosilane functionalization and silicone oil infusion to create SLIPS.
summary_en.result: The SLIPS on Ti6Al4V exhibited static water contact angles >105°, sliding angles <10°, and ice adhesion strength reduced to ~65 kPa with stable performance over repeated cycles.
summary_en.validation: Validation included contact angle goniometry, ice adhesion strength measurements (centrifugal method), and durability tests under mechanical abrasion, thermal exposure, and UV irradiation.

papers.title: Investigation of surface integrity in ultrasonic vibration-assisted minimum quantity lubrication milling of Ti-6Al-4V thin-walled parts
papers.first_author_affiliation: School of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Changsha University, Changsha, 410022, China

corresponding_authors.name: Yang Deng
corresponding_authors.affiliation: School of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Changsha University, Changsha, 410022, China

papers.venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是传统铣削加工，与增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper investigates surface integrity during conventional milling of Ti-6Al-4V, not a post-processing treatment for additive-manufactured Ti-6Al-4V. No connection to AM or post-processing routes like heat treatment, HIP, or surface finishing.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究超声振动辅助微量润滑铣削对Ti-6Al-4V薄壁件表面完整性的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用超声振动辅助微量润滑铣削实验，分析表面完整性参数。
summary_zh.result: 该工艺改善表面质量，降低表面粗糙度。
summary_zh.validation: 通过铣削实验验证表面完整性改善效果。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of ultrasonic vibration-assisted minimum quantity lubrication milling on the surface integrity of Ti-6Al-4V thin-walled parts.
summary_en.method: Experimental milling with ultrasonic vibration and minimum quantity lubrication, measuring surface roughness, residual stress, and microstructure.
summary_en.result: The process improves surface finish by reducing roughness and inducing favorable compressive residual stresses.
summary_en.validation: Validation through milling experiments and surface characterization.
